question: In the CIA triad, what does "confidentiality" mean?

options.A: Information is accessible only to authorised parties
options.B: Information is always available when users need it
options.C: Information is not changed without legitimate permission
options.D: Every user action can be traced back at a later time

question: An attacker alters a message in transit without being noticed. Which security property is mainly violated?

options.A: Confidentiality
options.B: Availability
options.C: Integrity
options.D: Anonymity

question: Which security property does a DDoS attack mainly target?

options.A: Confidentiality
options.B: Integrity
options.C: Availability
options.D: Non-repudiation

question: What does the principle of least privilege mean?

options.A: Every user gets administrator access so that work is faster
options.B: Users get only the permissions their task requires
options.C: Access is granted once and is never reviewed again
options.D: Only administrators are allowed to create new user accounts

question: How do threat, vulnerability and risk relate to each other?

options.A: A vulnerability is the party that intends to attack a system
options.B: A threat is a software weakness that has not been patched yet
options.C: Risk exists when a threat can exploit an asset's vulnerability
options.D: Risk is just another name for a vulnerability that was patched

question: What is meant by "defense in depth"?

options.A: Several layers of controls, so one failure does not expose everything
options.B: Relying on a single very strong perimeter firewall and using no other controls
options.C: Keeping the system design secret and making it the only form of protection
options.D: Handing every security control to one single team for the entire organisation

question: What characterises multi-factor authentication (MFA)?

options.A: Asking for two different passwords typed one after another by the user
options.B: Using one single password that is very long and very complex only
options.C: Asking for a password and then a security question answered by the user
options.D: Two or more different factor types, such as a password and a token

question: What is the difference between authentication and authorisation?

options.A: Authentication decides access rights; authorisation verifies the user's identity
options.B: Both are simply other terms for encrypting the user's passwords
options.C: Authentication applies only to devices; authorisation applies only to humans
options.D: Authentication verifies identity; authorisation decides access rights

question: What is the purpose of separation of duties?

options.A: Speeding up a process by handing every step over to a single person
options.B: Stopping one person from controlling every step of a critical process
options.C: Making sure that all employees have exactly the same access rights
options.D: Removing the need for audits of the company's financial processes

question: What does the 3-2-1 backup rule say?

options.A: Three copies of the data on the same single disk, tested twice a year
options.B: Three copies, two media types, one copy at a separate location
options.C: Two copies of the data on three media types with no off-site copy
options.D: One copy of the data updated three times a day on the same two servers

question: The default port for HTTPS is ...

options.A: TCP 8080
options.B: TCP 443
options.C: TCP 22
options.D: TCP 25

question: Which protocol provides remote shell access with encrypted traffic?

options.A: Telnet
options.B: FTP
options.C: HTTP
options.D: SSH

question: What is the main function of DNS?

options.A: Encrypting the traffic between a browser and a website
options.B: Giving IP addresses to devices automatically on a network
options.C: Translating domain names into IP addresses
options.D: Filtering packets according to their destination port number

question: What is the main function of DHCP?

options.A: Handing out IP configuration automatically to devices on a network
options.B: Translating domain names into IP addresses for browsers
options.C: Creating encrypted tunnels between two branch offices
options.D: Relaying email between mail servers across the whole internet

question: What is the main difference between TCP and UDP?

options.A: TCP is connection-oriented and guarantees delivery; UDP is connectionless with no guarantee
options.B: UDP is connection-oriented and guarantees delivery; TCP is connectionless with no guarantee
options.C: TCP is always encrypted, whereas UDP is never encrypted at all
options.D: They are exactly the same and differ only in the port number they use

question: In the TCP three-way handshake, which flags does the server's reply carry?

options.A: SYN and ACK together
options.B: SYN only, without ACK
options.C: FIN and ACK together
options.D: RST and ACK together

question: What is the difference between an IDS and an IPS?

options.A: An IPS only alerts; an IDS can block traffic directly
options.B: An IDS is for wireless networks only, whereas an IPS is for wired networks only
options.C: Both only work to filter spam email before it reaches the inbox
options.D: An IDS detects and alerts; an IPS can also block traffic directly

question: What is ARP spoofing?

options.A: Forging IP-to-MAC mappings on a LAN to redirect traffic
options.B: Forging DNS records on the authoritative server of the targeted domain
options.C: Flooding a server with SYN packets until it runs out of resources
options.D: Guessing an SSH password repeatedly until it finally succeeds

question: What is the main function of a VPN?

options.A: Guaranteeing that every site visited is free of malware and fraud
options.B: Creating an encrypted tunnel across an untrusted network
options.C: Adding physical bandwidth so that the connection is always faster
options.D: Erasing every trace of the user so that anonymity becomes absolute

question: What is a port scan used for?

options.A: Recovering a forgotten password on a server
options.B: Encrypting services so that their content cannot be read
options.C: Updating the firmware of network devices automatically
options.D: Finding out which ports and services are open on a host

question: What is the defining trait of symmetric encryption?

options.A: A public key for encryption and a private key for decryption
options.B: No key is used at all anywhere in the process
options.C: A new random key is made for every letter and then discarded
options.D: The same key is used for encryption and decryption

question: Which one is a public-key (asymmetric) cryptographic algorithm?

options.A: AES
options.B: SHA-256
options.C: RSA
options.D: HMAC

question: What is the key property of a cryptographic hash function?

options.A: Easy to reverse by using a secret key that only owners hold
options.B: Its output length grows along with the length of the input
options.C: Different inputs always produce exactly the same output value
options.D: One-way: easy to compute but impractical to invert

question: What is the purpose of a "salt" when storing passwords?

options.A: A random per-user value added before hashing, so equal passwords differ
options.B: A secret key used to decrypt the hash whenever the user logs in
options.C: A way of compressing hashes so that they fit into a small database
options.D: A way of sending passwords by email so that they are safe from sniffing

question: What does a digital signature provide?

options.A: Confidentiality of the message content and nothing else
options.B: Sender authenticity and message integrity
options.C: Compression of the message so that its size becomes smaller
options.D: A guarantee that the message will arrive more quickly

question: What is the essential function of a TLS digital certificate?

options.A: Binding a public key to its owner's identity, signed by a certificate authority
options.B: Storing the server administrator's password so that it is easy to recover again
options.C: Guaranteeing that the site in question is free of any malware and fraud
options.D: Encrypting the server's whole disk automatically every night of the week

question: Why is MD5 no longer suitable for digital signatures?

options.A: The algorithm is far too slow to be used on files of a very large size
options.B: The algorithm can only be used together with long symmetric keys
options.C: The algorithm produces output whose length keeps on changing all the time
options.D: Practical ways exist to make two inputs share one hash (collisions)

question: What is the benefit of forward secrecy in TLS?

options.A: The server's private key is never used while the connection is going on
options.B: Past sessions stay safe even if the server's private key leaks later on
options.C: Connection sessions never come to an end, so users always stay logged in
options.D: The server's certificate never expires even if left for many years

question: What does Kerckhoffs's principle state?

options.A: The encryption algorithm should be kept secret from the public so it is not studied
options.B: The encryption key may be announced as long as the algorithm stays secret
options.C: Security should rest on the key's secrecy, not the algorithm's
options.D: A complicated home-made algorithm is always safer than a standard one

question: Why is ECB mode discouraged for encrypting data?

options.A: The ciphertext it produces cannot be decrypted again by the owner of the key
options.B: This mode can only work for files whose size is below 1 KB in total
options.C: This mode needs both a public key and a private key at the same time
options.D: Identical blocks give identical ciphertext, so data patterns remain visible

question: What is SQL injection?

options.A: A script is inserted into a page so that the victim's browser runs it
options.B: User input is read as part of the SQL command, changing the query
options.C: The victim's browser is forced to send a request it did not intend
options.D: Another user's session ID is guessed repeatedly until it finally matches

question: The main defence against SQL injection is ...

options.A: Parameterised queries (prepared statements)
options.B: Only stripping single quotes out of the input
options.C: Only hiding database error messages from the users
options.D: Moving the database to another server without code changes

question: What is cross-site scripting (XSS)?

options.A: SQL commands are inserted into a form field on a certain website
options.B: A server is flooded with requests until it can no longer give any response
options.C: Malicious script injected into a page and run in the victim's browser
options.D: Password hashes are cracked by using rainbow tables prepared in advance

question: What is CSRF?

options.A: SQL commands are inserted through a URL parameter on a web page
options.B: A logged-in user's browser is forced to send an unwanted request
options.C: The site's DNS records are redirected so that they point to the attacker's server
options.D: Public Wi-Fi traffic is sniffed and its content is read by a third party

question: A common defence against CSRF is ...

options.A: Storing the users' passwords only in hashed form
options.B: Enabling gzip compression on all server responses
options.C: Random anti-CSRF tokens on data-changing requests
options.D: Limiting the URL length to at most 2048 characters only

question: What causes an IDOR (insecure direct object reference) vulnerability?

options.A: The TLS certificate belonging to that server expired a long time ago
options.B: The app accepts an object ID without checking the user's right to it
options.C: The server runs out of memory because too many sessions are open
options.D: Passwords are stored by using a hash algorithm that is considered weak

question: What does the HttpOnly cookie attribute do?

options.A: Forces the cookie to be sent only over a secure HTTPS connection
options.B: Deletes the cookie automatically when the browser is closed
options.C: Prevents JavaScript in the browser from reading that cookie
options.D: Restricts the cookie to one single specific subdomain only

question: What does Content-Security-Policy (CSP) do?

options.A: Encrypts the whole body of the response sent out by the server
options.B: Sets how long a page is kept in the cache of the browser
options.C: Sets the display language of that particular web page
options.D: Restricts which content sources a page may load, limiting XSS

question: What is the OWASP Top 10?

options.A: A list of the ten malware families that spread most widely around the world
options.B: A list of the most critical web application risk categories from OWASP
options.C: An encryption standard that must be used by all of the websites
options.D: A list of the ten countries with the largest number of cyberattacks

question: Where must input validation be done for it to be safe?

options.A: In browser JavaScript alone, since that is much faster
options.B: It is not needed if the site already uses HTTPS
options.C: On the server, because client-side checks can be bypassed
options.D: Only for input that comes from administrator accounts

question: What is phishing?

options.A: Tricking victims via seemingly legitimate messages into giving up credentials
options.B: Encrypting the files that belong to a victim and then asking a ransom for the key
options.C: Sending a great many data packets in order to knock a service offline
options.D: Scanning a network in order to look for open ports on the hosts

question: What is ransomware?

options.A: A program that silently records the keystrokes made by the user
options.B: Malware that spreads between computers by itself without any user action
options.C: A program that shows advertisements that the user does not want
options.D: Malware that encrypts a victim's data and demands payment for the key

question: What is the main difference between a worm and a virus?

options.A: A virus spreads itself over networks; a worm needs to attach to a file or program
options.B: A worm spreads itself over networks; a virus needs to attach to a file or program
options.C: A worm can only attack mobile devices and nothing else at all
options.D: They are exactly the same and differ only in their commercial names

question: What does a zero-day vulnerability mean?

options.A: An attack that can only take place at exactly 00:00 and no other time
options.B: A vulnerability that the vendor had already patched on the previous day
options.C: A vulnerability unknown to the vendor or not yet patched
options.D: An attack that does not cause any victims of any kind at all

question: What is social engineering?

options.A: Breaking encryption through very complicated mathematical computation
options.B: Modifying hardware chips before the device in question is sold
options.C: Manipulating people into leaking information or weakening security
options.D: An attack that can only be carried out by way of social media

question: What is credential stuffing?

options.A: Trying every combination of characters in sequence on one single account only
options.B: Inserting SQL commands into the login field of a website of some kind
options.C: Trying username and password pairs leaked from one service on other services
options.D: Forging a MAC address in order to impersonate some other device

question: What is a man-in-the-middle attack?

options.A: An attacker floods a server with requests coming from many sources at once
options.B: An attacker guesses passwords by using a list of commonly used words
options.C: An attacker copies data from a disk that someone has thrown away
options.D: An attacker secretly sits between two parties, reading or altering traffic

question: What does a keylogger do?

options.A: Records user keystrokes to steal information such as passwords
options.B: Encrypts files so that they cannot be opened by their rightful owner
options.C: Scans for the open ports that exist on a host in the network
options.D: Filters spam email before it gets to the inbox of the user

question: What is a botnet?

options.A: A single server that runs antivirus software for a whole office
options.B: A public Wi-Fi network that is provided by a café
options.C: A robot program that is used to legitimately test websites
options.D: A group of infected devices that an attacker controls remotely

question: What is privilege escalation?

options.A: Increasing the speed of the network connection that is in use
options.B: Adding to the number of legitimate users present on a system
options.C: Updating the operating system to the newest version available
options.D: Gaining higher access rights than one is supposed to have

question: What is the main function of a SIEM?

options.A: Collecting and correlating logs to detect security events
options.B: Encrypting the disks on all of the laptops that employees of a company use
options.C: Issuing TLS certificates for the websites that a company manages
options.D: Backing up the whole content of the company's databases every night

question: What is a CVE in information security?

options.A: A numeric score that expresses the severity level of a vulnerability
options.B: A standard identifier for publicly disclosed vulnerabilities
options.C: A kind of malware that specifically attacks databases
options.D: A professional certification meant for information security analysts

question: What is CVSS?

options.A: A standard system for rating vulnerability severity with a score from 0 to 10
options.B: A list of identifier numbers for vulnerabilities that are known to the public
options.C: A protocol for sending security logs between the collecting servers
options.D: An encryption standard for data that is stored in cloud services

question: What is MITRE ATT&CK?

options.A: A knowledge base of real-world adversary tactics and techniques
options.B: A numbered list of software vulnerabilities that have already been patched
options.C: A commercial antivirus product that is sold by the MITRE organisation
options.D: A certificate standard for securing the websites found on the internet

question: The correct order of incident response phases according to NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2 is ...

options.A: Containment; preparation; post-incident activity; detection and analysis; recovery
options.B: Post-incident activity; detection and analysis; preparation; containment, eradication
options.C: Preparation; detection-analysis; containment-eradication-recovery; post-incident
options.D: Recovery; containment; detection and analysis; preparation; post-incident activity

question: What is chain of custody in digital forensics?

options.A: A layered chain of encryption that protects the evidence files from access
options.B: A record of who held the evidence and when
options.C: The order in which patches are applied on a server that has been seized
options.D: A list of the culprits who are suspected of involvement in an incident

question: What is the goal of patch management?

options.A: Testing and applying updates to close vulnerabilities
options.B: Deleting every old log in order to save the storage space that is available
options.C: Replacing all of the hardware that the organisation owns every single year
options.D: Disabling all automatic updates so that the system stays stable

question: What is the key requirement for a penetration test to be legitimate?

options.A: Verbal permission from any employee of the target company is enough
options.B: No permission is needed as long as the results are reported later on
options.C: Written permission from the system owner with an agreed scope
options.D: It is carried out outside working hours so that nobody notices it

question: What does BSSN, the Indonesian government agency for cyber security, stand for?

options.A: Badan Sistem Siber Nasional
options.B: Balai Siber dan Sandi Nusantara
options.C: Badan Standar Sandi Nasional
options.D: Badan Siber dan Sandi Negara
